result.topic_en: Derivation of the differentials of right ascension and declination with respect to changes in ecliptic longitude, latitude and the obliquity of the ecliptic, applied to a small rotation (precession-type motion) of the reference system.
result.transcription:
Rekt. $\alpha$ $\lambda$ Länge
Decl. $\delta$ $\mathfrak{b}$ Breite
$\varepsilon$ Schiefe

Das Differential der Rectasc. $= (\cos\varepsilon + \sin\varepsilon\sin\alpha\,\mathrm{tg}\,\delta)\,\partial\lambda$
$- \frac{\sin\varepsilon\cos\alpha}{\cos\delta\cos\mathfrak{b}}\,\partial\mathfrak{b}$
$-$

$\partial\varepsilon = M\sin r\,\partial t$
$\mathfrak{b}$ fixi[?] $\partial\lambda = M\sin(\lambda+r)\tan\mathfrak{b}.\partial t$
$\partial\mathfrak{b} = M\cos(\lambda+r)\,.\partial t$

$\sin\alpha\cos\delta = \cos\varepsilon\sin\lambda\cos\mathfrak{b} - \sin\varepsilon$ [-...-] $\sin\mathfrak{b}$
$\cos\alpha\cos\delta = \cos\lambda\cos\mathfrak{b}$
$\sin\delta = \cos\varepsilon\sin\mathfrak{b} + \sin\varepsilon\sin\lambda\cos\mathfrak{b}$

fixi[?] $\partial\xi = M\sin r.\sin\mathfrak{b}\,\partial t = M\zeta\sin r\,\partial t$
$\partial\eta = -M\cos r\sin\mathfrak{b}.\partial t = -M\zeta\cos r\,\partial t$
$\partial\zeta = M\cos(\lambda+r)\cos\mathfrak{b}.\partial t = M(\eta\cos r - \xi\sin r)\partial t$

$\sin\alpha\cos\delta = x$ | $\sin\lambda\cos\mathfrak{b} = \xi$
$\cos\alpha\cos\delta = y$ | $\cos\lambda\cos\mathfrak{b} = \eta$
$\sin\delta = z$ | $\sin\mathfrak{b} = \zeta$

$\frac{\partial\alpha}{\partial t} = \frac{M}{\cos\delta^2}\left\{\begin{array}{l} y\zeta\cos\varepsilon\sin r \\ +x\zeta\cos r \\ -y\eta\sin\varepsilon\cos r \\ +y\xi\sin\varepsilon\sin r\end{array}\right\} - yz\sin r$

$x = \xi\cos\varepsilon - \zeta\sin\varepsilon$ | $\xi = x\cos\varepsilon + z\sin\varepsilon$
$y = \eta$ | $\eta = y$
$z = \xi\sin\varepsilon + \zeta\cos\varepsilon$ | $\zeta = -x\sin\varepsilon + z\cos\varepsilon$

$-xx\sin\varepsilon + xz\cos\varepsilon$
$-yy\sin\varepsilon$

$= \frac{M}{\cos\delta^2}\left\{[-yz\sin r-] - ((xx+yy)\sin\varepsilon - xz\cos\varepsilon)\cos r\right\}$
$= M\cos r\left\{-\sin\varepsilon - \sin\alpha\tan\delta\cos\varepsilon\right\}$

$\frac{\partial x}{\partial\varepsilon} = -z$ | $\frac{\partial x}{\partial\xi} = \cos\varepsilon$ | $\frac{\partial x}{\partial\eta} = 0$ | $\frac{\partial x}{\partial\zeta} = -\sin\varepsilon$
$\frac{\partial y}{\partial\varepsilon} = 0$ | $\frac{\partial y}{\partial\xi} = 0$ | $\frac{\partial y}{\partial\eta} = 1$ | $\frac{\partial y}{\partial\zeta} = 0$
$\frac{\partial z}{\partial\varepsilon} = x$ | $\frac{\partial z}{\partial\xi} = \sin\varepsilon$ | $\frac{\partial z}{\partial\eta} = 0$ | $\frac{\partial z}{\partial\zeta} = \cos\varepsilon$

$\partial\delta = \frac{x\partial\varepsilon + \sin\varepsilon\partial\xi + \cos\varepsilon\partial\zeta}{\cos\delta}$
$= \frac{M\partial t}{\cos\delta}\left\{\begin{array}{l} x\sin r \quad +\eta\cos r\cos\varepsilon \\ +\zeta\sin\varepsilon\sin r - \xi\sin r\cos\varepsilon\end{array}\right\}$
$= \frac{M\partial t}{\cos\delta}\{y\cos r\cos\varepsilon\}$

$\partial x = y\partial\alpha - \sin\alpha.z.\partial\delta$ | $\partial\xi = \eta\partial\lambda - \sin\lambda.\zeta.\partial\mathfrak{b}$
$\partial y = -x\partial\alpha - \cos\alpha.z\,\partial\delta$ | $\partial\eta = -\xi\partial\lambda - \cos\lambda.\zeta\partial\mathfrak{b}$
$\partial z = \cos\delta\,\partial\delta$ | $+\cos\mathfrak{b}.\partial\mathfrak{b}$

$\frac{y\partial x - x\partial y}{\cos}$
$\partial\alpha = \frac{y\partial x - x\partial y}{\cos\delta^2}$
$\partial\delta = \frac{\partial z}{\cos\delta}$

$\frac{\partial\alpha}{\partial t} = -M\cos r\{\sin\varepsilon + \cos\varepsilon\sin\alpha\,\mathrm{tg}\,\delta\}$
$\frac{\partial\delta}{\partial t} = M\cos r\{\cos\varepsilon\cos\alpha\}$

$\partial\alpha = \frac{-yz\,\partial\varepsilon + y\cos\varepsilon\,\partial\xi - x\partial\eta - y\sin\varepsilon\,\partial\zeta}{\cos\delta^2}$
$= \frac{-yz\,\partial\varepsilon + (\eta y\cos\varepsilon + \xi x)\partial\lambda - (y\cos\varepsilon\sin\lambda\sin\mathfrak{b} - x\cos\lambda\sin\mathfrak{b} + y\sin\varepsilon\cos\mathfrak{b})\,\partial\mathfrak{b}}{\cos\delta^2}$
$= \frac{-(\eta\xi\sin\varepsilon + \eta\zeta\cos\varepsilon)\partial\varepsilon + ((\xi\xi+\eta\eta)\cos\varepsilon - \xi\zeta\sin\varepsilon)\partial\lambda - \sin\varepsilon\cos\lambda\,\partial\mathfrak{b}}{\cos\delta^2}$
